newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 6.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Following a revision of the Criminal Procedure Law, concerns are rising over human right's abuses. Thirty-two out of 65 suspects have been arrested this year under the 'Emergency Arrest System' which does not require the prior issuance of an arrest warrant.
- The United States government will reportedly soon resume sending an additional $6 million worth of aid to North Korea following Pyongyang's apology for the submarine incursion.

- In its third day of nation-wide strikes, the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) announced plans for an all-out strike in 20 major cities including Seoul starting from January 6, by 230,000 union members.

- The Prosecution Office is seeking to arrest key leaders of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) and Federation of Korean Trade Unions (FKTU), including KCTU committee chairman, Kwon Young Gil.

- For the first time after its official apology, North Korea will reportedly send a representative group to participate in the international seminar '21st Century and the Status of Mankind', to be held in Tokyo from February 7.
